title: Places of worship
examples: Why do you take your shoes off in a temple?

explain.say: Every faith has special buildings where people gather to pray, worship and learn. Here are six: the mandir, the church, the mosque, the synagogue, the gurdwara and the Buddhist stupa or temple.
Each building has a name and a heart, the special thing at its centre. Let's see them side by side.

items: Mandir | Hindu | Shrine with murtis, sacred images of deities
Mosque | Muslim | Mihrab showing the direction of Mecca
Synagogue | Jewish | Ark holding the Torah scrolls
Gurdwara | Sikh | Guru Granth Sahib, the scripture
Stupa or temple | Buddhist | Relics or a Buddha image

explain.say: In a mosque, Muslims pray in rows facing Mecca, and they wash before prayer. In a synagogue, Jews read from the Torah scrolls kept in the Ark, with an eternal light burning above it.

a: Minaret for the call to prayer

explain.say: A gurdwara means the doorway to the Guru. Sikhs cover their heads and sit before the Guru Granth Sahib, and every gurdwara has a langar, a free kitchen where anyone of any faith can share a meal, sitting together as equals.

items: Bow before the Guru Granth Sahib

draw.text: The Golden Temple in Amritsar has four doors: open to people from every direction.

explain.say: In a mandir, Hindus offer puja, worship with flowers, food and the waving of lamps called arti. In a church, Christians gather for prayer, hymns and Holy Communion. At a stupa, Buddhists walk around it clockwise in quiet reflection.

draw.text: Stupa: Buddhists walk around it clockwise.

explain.say: Different as they look, most places of worship share a lot: a quiet space, signs of respect like removing shoes or covering the head, a sacred text or symbol, and a community that comes together.

items: A space set apart and kept quiet
Signs of respect: shoes off, head covered
A sacred text, image or symbol
Teaching, charity and food for others

faq.a: A gurdwara is a Sikh place of worship; the name means the doorway to the Guru. Inside, the Sikh scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, rests on a raised platform under a canopy. Every gurdwara has a langar, a free community kitchen open to everyone.
asks: what do Sikhs do in a gurdwara

faq.a: Langar is the free kitchen in every gurdwara. Volunteers cook and serve a simple vegetarian meal to anyone, whatever their faith, wealth or background, and people sit together on the floor as equals. It was begun by Guru Nanak to teach equality and service.
asks: why do gurdwaras give free food
free food at the Sikh temple

faq.a: A mandir is a Hindu temple. At its heart is a shrine holding murtis, sacred images of deities, and worshippers offer puja with flowers, food, incense and the waving of lamps called arti. Many Hindus also worship at a shrine at home.
asks: what is inside a Hindu temple

faq.a: A mosque has a prayer hall with no chairs, where people pray in rows facing Mecca. A niche in the wall called the mihrab shows that direction, the minbar is the pulpit for the Friday sermon, and there is a place to wash before prayer. Many mosques have a dome and a minaret.
asks: what do Muslims do in a mosque

faq.a: A synagogue is a Jewish house of prayer, study and community. The Torah scrolls are kept in a cabinet called the Ark, with an eternal light above, and they are read aloud from a raised platform called the bimah, especially on Shabbat.

Most churches have an altar or communion table at the front, a cross, a font or pool for baptism, a pulpit or lectern for reading the Bible, and seats for the congregation. Large ones led by a bishop are called cathedrals.

A stupa is a dome-shaped Buddhist monument, often holding relics of the Buddha or of great teachers. Buddhists walk around it clockwise while praying or meditating. In East Asia the stupa grew into the tall tiered tower called a pagoda.

faq.q: Why do people take off their shoes in a temple?
faq.a: Removing shoes is a sign of respect and of keeping the sacred space clean. Shoes are removed in mandirs, mosques, gurdwaras and Buddhist temples. In churches and synagogues people usually keep their shoes on.
asks: why do you remove shoes in a mosque

faq.q: Why do Muslims face Mecca when they pray?
faq.a: Muslims face the Kaaba in Mecca, called the qibla direction, so that all Muslims worldwide pray facing the same point, a sign of unity. The Kaaba is not worshipped; Muslims worship God alone.

faq.q: Why do people cover their heads in a gurdwara?
faq.a: Covering the head is a sign of respect before the Guru Granth Sahib, so everyone in a gurdwara, Sikh or not, covers their head. Many Jewish men wear a kippah in the synagogue for a similar reason of respect before God.
asks: why wear a headscarf in a gurdwara
head covering in places of worship

faq.q: Can anyone visit a place of worship?
faq.a: Usually yes. Most mandirs, churches, mosques, synagogues, gurdwaras and temples welcome respectful visitors, and many run open days for schools. It helps to dress modestly, follow the customs about shoes and head covering, and ask before taking photos.
asks: can non Muslims go into a mosque

faq.a: Jains worship in temples often called derasars, Shinto followers visit shrines marked by a torii gate, Zoroastrians pray in fire temples where a sacred fire is kept burning, and Bahá'í houses of worship have nine sides and are open to all.

faq.q: Do you have to go to a place of worship to be religious?
faq.a: Not always. Many people pray at home or wherever they are; Hindus often have home shrines, and Muslims may pray anywhere that is clean. Still, gathering together matters in most faiths, such as Friday prayers for Muslims, Shabbat for Jews and Sunday services for many Christians.

facts: Gurdwara means the doorway to the Guru; every gurdwara has a langar, a free kitchen open to all.
In a mosque, the mihrab is a niche showing the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca.
In a synagogue, the Torah scrolls are kept in the Ark, with an eternal light, the ner tamid, above it.
The Golden Temple in Amritsar, the Harmandir Sahib, has four entrances, a sign that it is open to all.
Buddhists walk clockwise around a stupa, a dome-shaped monument that often holds relics.

options.show: They are signs of respect for a sacred space
options.say: They are signs of respect for a sacred space
